Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 90, verses 1–10:

Meccan. It has three hundred and twenty letters, eighty-two words, and twenty verses.

Nafil ibn Arḍam ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us, saying:

ʿAmr ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Sabat ibn al-Yasaʿ related to us, saying: Yahya ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Sulami related to us, saying: Abu ʿIsma Nuh ibn Abi Maryam related to us, from ʿAli ibn Zayd, from Zirr, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿I swear by this city﴾ Allah will grant him security from His anger on the Day of Resurrection" [147] [[Tafsir Majmaʿ al-Bayan: 10/357.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿I swear by this city﴾ means: I swear by this city, meaning Makkah, ﴿and you, O Muhammad, are a resident (ḥill) in this city﴾, meaning you may do as you wish in it, of killing and taking captive. The reason is that Allah, glorified is He, made Makkah lawful (ḥalal) for His Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of the conquest, so that he fought and killed, and He made lawful what He willed and forbade what He willed. He killed Ibn Khatal while he was clinging to the curtains of the Kaʿbah, and Muqayyis ibn Subabah and others. Then he said: "Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe," so he made lawful the blood of Ibn Khatal and his companions and forbade the house of Abu Sufyan. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah made Makkah sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred until the Hour rises. It was not made lawful for anyone before me, nor will it be made lawful for anyone after me, and it was made lawful for me only for an hour of a day. Its trees are not to be cut, its grass is not to be uprooted, its game is not to be frightened, and its lost property is not to be taken except by one who announces it."

Then al-ʿAbbas said: "O Messenger of Allah, except the idhkhir, for it is for our goldsmiths and our graves and our houses." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Except the idhkhir" [148] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/253, with variation.]].

Shurahbil ibn Saʿd said regarding His words ﴿and you are a resident in this city﴾: They forbid you to kill game in it or cut a tree in it, yet they consider it lawful to expel you and kill you. ﴿And the begetter and what he begot﴾: ʿIkrimah and Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: "the begetter" is the one who has offspring, and "what he begot" is the barren one who has no offspring. This was related from Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿAli. This view makes "má" (what) remain [as a relative pronoun], and it would be ... (the text reads: "wa-huwa yuʿbad" [[As it stands in the manuscript.]]) and it is not sound except with an implied element. ʿAtiyyah, from him: the begetter and his offspring.

Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Abu Salih: ﴿the begetter﴾ is Adam, ﴿and what he begot﴾ is his offspring.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Burhan ibn ʿAli related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Walid al-ʿUkbari related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi related to us, saying: Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān related to us, saying: I heard Abu ʿImran al-Khawli recite ﴿wa-wālidin wa-mā walad﴾ and Ibrahim said: "wa-mā walad" (with fatha on the lam, "what was begotten"). ﴿We have indeed created man in kabad﴾, meaning in toil.

From al-Walibi, from Ibn ʿAbbas: al-Hasan said: he struggles with the calamities of this world and the hardships of the Hereafter. Qatadah: in hardship, so he does not meet anything except that he struggles with the matter of this world and the Hereafter. Saʿid ibn Jubayr: in hardship. From al-Hasan also: he struggles to give thanks in ease and to be patient in adversity, and he is never free of either. ʿAtiyyah from Ibn ʿAbbas: in the hardship of his creation: his carrying, his birth, his nursing, his weaning, his livelihood, his life and his death. ʿAmr ibn Dinar from him: the growth of his teeth. Yaman: Allah has not created a creature that struggles as the son of Adam struggles, and he is, with all that, the weakest of creatures. And from Saʿid ibn Jubayr also: in the straitness of his livelihood. Ibn Kaysan: al-mukabadah is enduring a matter and bearing its greatest part, and its root is hardship, and it derives from kabad. Labid said:

"O eye, why did you not weep for Arbad... when we stood and the adversaries stood in kabad" [[Lisan al-ʿArab: 3/376.]]

Mujahid, Ibrahim, ʿIkrimah, ʿAbd Allah ibn Shaddad, ʿAtiyyah and al-Dahhak said: it means upright, standing, of balanced stature. This is the report of Muqatil from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Every creature that walks on the earth walks on four, except man, who was created upright, standing on two legs. Muqatil: in strength. It was revealed concerning Ibn al-Asadayn, whose name was Usayd ibn Kaldah ibn Usayd ibn Khalaf. He was strong and powerful, and he would place a leather mat of ʿUkaz under his feet and say: "Whoever removes me from it, for him is such and such." It could not be pulled from under his feet except in pieces, and the place of his foot would remain. It is also said: it means the hardship of command and prohibition, and of reward and punishment. Ibn Zayd said: ﴿We have indeed created man﴾ means Adam, ﴿in kabad﴾, meaning in the middle of the sky, at the time he was raised to Paradise. Abu Bakr al-Warraq: meaning he cannot reach his desire nor attain his aim. Khusayf said regarding its meaning: the struggle and the transition through the states of the drop, then the clinging clot, until the complete completion of creation. Ibn Kaysan: he stands upright with his head; when Allah, glorified is He, permits his expulsion, his head turns to the feet of his mother. It is also said: bold of heart, hard of liver, with weakness of constitution and lowliness of substance.

Jaʿfar: meaning in trial and affliction.

Ibn ʿAta: in darkness and ignorance.

Muhammad ibn ʿAli al-Tirmidhi: neglecting what concerns him and occupied with what does not concern him.

﴿Does he think﴾, meaning by his strength: ﴿that no one will have power over him﴾, meaning Allah, glorified and exalted is He. It is also said: he is al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. Abu al-Duha informed me from Ibn ʿAbbas. ﴿He says: I have squandered﴾, meaning I have spent wealth, ﴿lubadan﴾, piled one upon another, and it derives from talabbud in enmity toward Muhammad.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn ʿAmir ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manaf, because he committed a sin and sought a ruling from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who ordered him to expiate, and he said: "My wealth has gone in expiations and expenditures since I entered the religion of Muhammad."

The readers differed concerning His words lubadan. Abu Jaʿfar read it with a shaddah on the ba', as the plural of labid and raki (a form such as "rukkaʿ"). Mujahid read it with a damma on the lam and the ba', unstressed, as in your saying: "amr bakr" and "rajul junub." The rest read it with a damma on the lam and a fatha on the ba', unstressed. It has two meanings: the first is the plural of lubdah, and the second is in the singular, like Qutham and Hutham, and it is not an altered form.

﴿Does he think that no one has seen him﴾, meaning Allah, glorified is He; it is also said: Muhammad (peace be upon him). So he would know the amount of his expenditure, and he was lying, as he did not spend all that he claimed. Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Qatadah said: Does he think that no one has seen him, so that he would be asked about this wealth, from where he acquired it and where he spent it?

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: ʿUmar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi related to us, saying: al-Haytham ibn Khalaf al-Duri related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Sulayman, mawla of Bani Hashim, related to me, saying: Husayn ibn al-Husayn, that is al-Ashqar, related to us, saying: Hisham ibn Shabr related to us, from Abu Hashim, from Mukhalid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The feet of the servant will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about four things: about his life, how he spent it; about his wealth, from where he acquired it and how he spent it; about his knowledge, what he did with it; and about our love for the People of the House" [149] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 14/379, no. 39012, 39013.]].

Ibn Kharijah said: I have not heard this hadith except from al-Haytham.

Husayn informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan ʿAli ibn Harun ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Musa ibn Harun ibn ʿAbd Allah related to us, saying: Abu al-Rabiʿ al-Zahrani related to us, saying: Nuʿaym ibn Maysarah related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz informed me, saying: a man from Bani ʿAmir informed me, from his father, who said: I prayed behind the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and I heard him recite: ﴿Does he think that no one will have power over him?﴾ ﴿Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾, with a kasrah on the sin (yahsibu).

﴿Did We not make for him two eyes, and a tongue, and two lips?﴾ Qatadah said: Yes, by Allah, they are consistent in overpowering you with them, concealing gratitude.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmir al-Samarqandi informed us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Jaghwayh related to us, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Madani related to us, from Abu Hazim, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Son of Adam, if your tongue contends with you concerning what I have forbidden you, then I have helped you against it with two lids, so close them. If your eye contends with you toward some of what I have forbidden you, then I have helped you against it with two lids, so close them. If your private part contends with you toward what I have forbidden you, then I have helped you against it with two lids, so close them" [150] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/65; and in Kanz al-ʿUmmal with variation: 15/856, no. 43407.]].

﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾. Most of the exegetes said: meaning We made clear to him the path of good and evil, truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, like His words: ﴿Indeed We guided him to the way, whether he be grateful or ungrateful﴾ [[Surah al-Insan: 3.]].

The evidence for this interpretation is what

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed me, by ijazah, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, from Qurrah ibn Khalid, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "They are only two highways: the highway of good and the highway of evil, so what makes the highway of evil dearer to you than the highway of good?" [151] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/256.]].

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Bishr related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq related to us, saying: my father related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Abi Bakr al-Qurashi, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words, glorified is He: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾, who said: "the two breasts." This view was taken by Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab and al-Dahhak. And najd is a raised path. The poet said:

"In the morning they went, and you asked about the valley of Nakhlah, and another of them was a crier on the highway of Kabkab" [[al-Sihah: 2/542.]].

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 90, verse 11–20:

Then he did not attempt the steep climb (al-'aqabah). That is, this human being did not traverse the steep path, so as to command (the good).

Al-Farra' said: He mentioned ﴿فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ﴾ with "lā" once. The Arabs rarely use "lā" alone with the past tense verb in such a position, except that they repeat it in another sentence, as in: ﴿Neither did he believe nor did he pray﴾ and ﴿No fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾. He did this here only because the latter part of the speech shows its meaning, so it was not necessary to repeat it. For he explained the "attempting of the steep climb" with several things, saying: ﴿freeing a slave﴾ and so on. It is as if he had said at the beginning: "So he did neither this nor that nor that."

Some of them said: The meaning of the speech is interrogative, its estimated form being "Then did he not attempt the steep climb?" This is the view of Ibn Zayd and a group of exegetes. The meaning: "Why did he not spend his wealth on freeing slaves and feeding the hungry, so that he might cross the steep path by it, and that would be better for him than spending it on enmity toward Muhammad." It is said that he compared the greatness of sin and its heaviness on its perpetrator to a steep path; so when he frees a slave and does righteous deeds, his likeness is that of one who has attempted that steep path, which is the sins, until they depart and melt away, like one who climbs a steep path, stands upon it, and similar.

It is reported from Ibn Imran that this steep path is a mountain in Hell. Ka'b said: it is seventy levels in Hell. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it is a difficult steep path in the Fire, short of the bridge, so cross it by obedience to Allah the Exalted. Mujahid, al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: it is the Sirat, laid over Hell like the edge of a sword, a distance of three thousand (years), uphill, downhill and level, and on its two sides are hooks and grapples like the thorns of al-sa'dan. So there is one who is saved and safe, one who is torn and wounded, and one who is thrown headlong into the Fire. Some pass over it like a flash of lightning, some like a violent wind, some like a rider, some like a man walking, some crawl crawling, and among them are those who slip and stumble, and some who are thrown into the Fire. Its crossing for the believer is like the time between the afternoon prayer and the night prayer.

Qatadah said: This is a parable which Allah the Exalted has struck: it means that the one who frees and feeds struggles with his soul and his Satan, like one who labours to climb a steep path. Ibn Zayd said: it means, "Why did he not take the path in which lies salvation and good?" Then He explained what it is, saying:

﴿It is freeing a slave﴾: whoever frees a slave, that (act) will be his ransom from the Fire. Abu Raja', al-Hasan, Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i read "fakka" and "raqabah" with the fatha on the kaf and mim, as a verb, like in ﴿thumma kana﴾. Then He informed what it is, saying: ﴿freeing a slave﴾. ﴿Or feeding on a day of hunger (masghabah)﴾, that is, a time of famine.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Halabi say: I heard Abu Hamid al-Khazraji say: "Al-matrabah" here derives from "al-turbah," which is severity of condition. The Hudhali poet recited:

"And when a guest alighted in our land, we shed the blood of camels in the dust of wealth."
[Lisan al-'Arab: 11/191.]

al-Hasan informed me, saying: 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ishaq al-Ansari narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us from Talhah ibn Musarrif from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awsajah from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me a deed that will enter me into Paradise." It was said: the meaning of the hamzah form is "mutbiqah" (sealed), and the form without hamzah is "mughlaqah" (locked); and from it the door is called "wasid."
